 Warriors roll to sixth straight victory, Curry scorches Heat as Splash Bros reunite 
 Curry cooks the Heat in second half, Warriors win sixth in a row

 Miami Heat’s Bam Adebayo (13) chats with Golden State Warriors’ Stephen Curry (30) after their NBA game at Chase Center in San Francisco, Calif., on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. The Golden State Warriors defeated the Miami Heat 120-100. (Jose Carlos Fajardo/Bay Area News Group) 
 By Joseph Dycus | jdycus@bayareanewsgroup.com | Bay Area News Group PUBLISHED: November 5, 2026 at 9:37 PM PST | UPDATED: November 6, 2026 at 7:45 AM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... SAN FRANCISCO – Steph Curry shook onetime Splash Bro Klay Thompson on a nasty cut midway through the first quarter, deking him on the same move the two terrorized the league with for over a decade together.
 But he smoked the layup against his teammate of 11 years, one of eight misses he suffered in the first half. It was another slow start.
 But just as he did in Denver in late October and against Phoenix on Monday, Curry turned it up in the third quarter of Golden State’s 120-100 victory over the Heat at Chase Center on Thursday.
 Curry scored 14 points in the third after going just 2-of-10 in the first half, and finished with 29 points in just 28 minutes as the Warriors figured out Miami’s zone defense and ran off their sixth victory in a row.
 “I think you start to get a feel for the game and the idea of understanding where your spots are going to be,” Curry said. “And we all know I love the endurance of being able to kind of withstand pressure for the whole game and knowing I’ll hopefully eventually find my way.”
 It was the continuation of a winning run that began after Golden State dropped its third game in a row to begin the season. Doubt had begun to creep in.
 That’s when head coach Steve Kerr gave a pep talk to the team that was part motivational and half encouragement.
 “We were really close to being able to put together, you know, winning performances and the Memphis game, again besides the last four minutes, the way that those guys played in Phoenix and then how we’ve been playing since, it’s just small building blocks of an identity,” Kerr remembered.
 Curry has been on a heater since then, scoring at least 24 in each of his last four games.
 “He just mentioned sticking with the process and the things that he noticed on film and just the feel in games,” Curry remembered.
Thursday night, he passed Oscar Robertson for 17th all-time on the NBA’s scoring list by scoring his 16,711th point on a 3-pointer.
 Curry’s second-half flurries might mystify defenses, but teammate De’Anthony Melton casually shrugged when explaining the outbursts.
 “He’s been doing that for 18 years,” Melton said. “When it was 2017, those third-quarter Warriors, they were the greatest team to ever play basketball. So it ain’t no different. Steph is Steph. I don’t know what he does to get himself going … but he’s just feeling things out, seeing how his shot is feeling, and then he makes adjustments.”
 Despite Curry’s slow start, the Warriors were tied 53-53 at halftime. They received big contributions from multiple players. By the final buzzer, Gary Payton scored nine and Georges Niang put up 10 as the bench combined to score 51. Will Richard scored 10 in a surprise start while Brandin Podziemski had another well-rounded performance with nine points and six rebounds. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg put up 17 points.
 Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 20 points and 14 rebounds while Bam Adebayo had 18 points and 10 rebounds for the Heat. Andrew Wiggins scored just two points on 1-of-6 shooting.
 The Warriors (6-3) will have one day off before facing the Magic on Saturday.
 Klay Thompson returns to Chase Center 
 Golden State Warriors’ De'Anthony Melton (8) drives past Miami Heat's Klay Thompson (11) in the first quarter of their NBA game at Chase Center in San Francisco, Calif., on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. (Jose Carlos Fajardo/Bay Area News Group)  
 Warriors coach Steve Kerr noted during the pregame press conference that as odd as it was to see Thompson and Wiggins in another uniform, such is life in the NBA for all but a handful of lifers.
 But even though Thompson and Wiggins have made several appearances in San Francisco since leaving the Bay Area, the hometown crowd still welcomed them back.
 Thompson, who received loud cheers during his pregame introduction, stepped foot in Chase Center playing like the flamethrower who once made an NBA-record 14 3-pointers as a member of the Warriors.
 He scored 30 points and buried the game-winner against the Clippers on Wednesday, the latest in a string of high-scoring performances.
 “He’s shooting the ball well right now, and the last few games, they bring him off screens, you know, just like we did,” Kerr said pregame.
 Thompson could not reach those same shooting heights against the Warriors, but he did finish with 11 points. He even got Curry on a nice pump fake before burying the 3-pointer, but also got burned a few times himself.
 “That was fun. It was really fun,” Thompson said. “You know, Steph is super crafty, still to this day. It felt good to block his shot. He made a great up-and-under on me. He had an incredible night. What he’s doing, I might have not appreciated it as much as his teammate because I got to see it every night so it became normal, so to see it as an opponent is incredible.”
 Draymond Green, Al Horford hold own against Heat star duo 
 Miami Heat's Bam Adebayo (13) is fouled by Golden State Warriors’ Charles Bassey (28) in the second quarter of their NBA game at Chase Center in San Francisco, Calif., on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. (Jose Carlos Fajardo/Bay Area News Group)  
 Draymond Green and Al Horford might not fly around as they did as 20-somethings in the 2010s, but both Warriors bigs were able to make positive contributions against the Heat’s star duo of Antetokounmpo and Adebayo.

 It was a bit of redemption for Green, who was ejected from Monday’s game against Phoenix after throwing Khaman Maluach to the floor and grabbing Dillon Brooks.
 “That’s just gonna happen sometimes, like I was sending my message,” Green said, later explaining what happened with Brooks. “He came in talking, putting his shoulder on my chest. You know that ain’t how you de-escalate. I wish he stood on the type of business he was on instead of running to y’all saying ‘I was trying to de-escalate.'”
 Green put up 11 assists – his best being a full-court pass to Curry for a layup – and made sure to challenge Miami’s MVP candidate Antetokounmpo anytime he tried to drive into the paint. Green also had five rebounds.
 Horford put in eight points and four rebounds in 18 minutes. His best play? A shocking reverse putback layup from the 40-year-old in the third quarter.
